title: New Expensify
description: Build an expense-report learning app with validation, workflow transitions, category totals, local chat, settings, and persistent local state.
problem: Learners need a source-grounded way to understand and extend New Expensify while separating implemented behavior from demo data, simulations, and missing integrations.
audience: Third-year undergraduate students who have completed introductory programming and want a practical mobile mini-project.
prerequisites: Git basics and ability to run the platform tooling described in the source README
learning_outcomes: Explain and trace expense and report types, seed records, and derived totals in its named source files.
Explain and trace positive amount/title validation, category aggregation, and money formatting in its named source files.
Explain and trace allowed status transitions, submission preconditions, and immutable updates in its named source files.
Explain and trace message append, trimming/search, and conversation display in its named source files.
Explain and trace context initialization, asyncstorage adapter, store keys, hydration and effects in its named source files.
Explain and trace navigation tabs, shared controls/theme, action wiring, and ui status in its named source files.
Explain and trace unit coverage, test command, pii sensitivity, and runtime evidence in its named source files.
Distinguish unit-test evidence from device, service, and deployment evidence.
Propose a safe, bounded extension without describing it as already implemented.
